title: Fastest courier route
prompt:
A courier firm has vans waiting at several depots, and every van leaves at minute 0. The city has n addresses numbered 0 to n − 1. Each road [a, b, minutes] is one-way: a van at address a reaches b after that many minutes. For every address, return the earliest minute any van could arrive there, or -1 if no van can reach it. A depot's own answer is 0.

- 1 <= n <= 10,000; 0 to 50,000 roads; 1 <= minutes <= 1,000.
- depots holds 1 to n addresses and may repeat one. Roads may repeat or form cycles.
hints: Every travel time is positive, so the address with the smallest arrival time that is not yet fixed can never be improved later. That is Dijkstra's algorithm.
There is no need to run Dijkstra once per depot. Put every depot in the heap at time 0 and run it once.
When you pop an address that already has an answer, the entry is stale: skip it.

solution.explanation: This is Dijkstra with many sources. Every depot enters a min-heap at time 0. Each pop gives the unsettled address with the smallest arrival time; because travel times are positive, nothing found later can beat it, so it is fixed. Its outgoing roads then push arrival times for unsettled neighbours. Addresses never popped stay -1.

complexity.notes: Each road pushes at most one heap entry, and each push or pop costs O(log m). The adjacency list and the heap take O(n + m) space.

followUps: Also return which depot serves each address.
Some roads are closed during rush hour. How would you handle travel times that depend on the time you set off?
